 Suit For Damages On Account Of False &
 Malicious Prosecution & Damages
Judgment:

1. The present suit has been filed by the plaintiffs with the submissions that they and their families are highly respectable in the society and enjoy very good reputation among the public, relatives and friends in the society and also in the estimation of General Public and Society at large.

It is averred that the families of the parties are close relatives and the defendants are persons of pusillanimous &
quarrelsome nature and have envy and jealousy with the plaintiff's family so they have been harassing them in various manners including by falsely and groundlessly dragging and implicating them in false, malicious, baseless, groundless, frivolous and vexatious litigation in the course of law.

It is averred that deceased Smt. Rambati @ Bittan, daughter of defendant no. 1 and 2 and sister of defendant no. 3 was married to deceased Sh. Raj Kumar, son of plaintiff no. 1 and 2 and brother of plaintiff no. 3 around in year 1988 in a very simple manner and without any exchange of dowry by anyone.
It is averred that plaintiff no. 3 was a child aged about hardly 3 years at the time of marriage.
It is averred that due to misbehavior and misconduct of Sh. Raj Kumar, plaintiff no. 1 and 2 debarred him during his lifetime so he begins to reside separately from the plaintiffs since a long.
It is averred that due to misunderstanding, his wife along with her children left the company of her husband Raj Kumar and began to reside with the plaintiffs at their house.

1.1 It is averred that an unfortunate alleged incident occurred on 26.10.2007 between Sh. Raj Kumar and his wife Smt. Rambati @ Bittan and she died and a criminal case bearing FIR No. 1491/2007,
dated 26.10.2007 was registered at PS Sultanpuri for the incident and during the course of investigation, Sh. Raj Kumar was arrested.

It is averred that on 28.10.2007 during the investigation,
the defendants deliberately, knowingly and intentionally made false statements to the police and twisted the matter of harassment for dowry and falsely implicated the plaintiffs also without any reasonable ground, cause and justification.
It is averred that consequently the police had to invoke Section 498 A IPC also and filed the chargesheet against the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs were granted anticipatory bail by the court.

It is averred that not only this but during the trial also, the defendants falsely, deliberately, knowingly and intentionally made false statements regarding harassment for dowry without any reasonable ground.

It is averred that vide order dated 24.04.2008, the Ld. Court finding no case of offence punishable under Section 302 IPC against the plaintiffs graciously pleased to discharge them at the stage of framing of charge and while pronouncing the judgment dated 23.10.2013, Ld. Court honourably acquitted the plaintiffs of all the charges.

It is averred that thus the plaintiffs' malicious and false prosecution has successfully terminated in their favour and the defendants' malice, ulterior motive and intention of their false implication and prosecution has been proved beyond reasonable doubt and the aforesaid order and judgment have attained finality by the efflux of time.

1.2 It is averred that during the period of investigation trial of aforesaid false and malicious case at the defendants' behest the plaintiffs have not only suffered from and undergone a tremendous harassment, agony, insult and humiliation but they have to also incur heavy amount of money in defending themselves in the case without their fault and involvement.

It is averred that not only this Om Prakash Tomar Ors vs Deshpal Singh on 31 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82777668/

It is averred that the plaintiffs have suffered a huge amount of pecuniary and mental loss, though the same cannot be calculable however, they quantify this loss in the sum of Rs. 9 lac.
2.

The suit is opposed by the defendants who filed their joint written statement averring that suit is liable to be dismissed with heavy cost as no cause of action has been arisen to file the same and that the same is filed to blackmail them.
It is averred that Ld. Judge opined that the possibility of won over of the witness who was residing with her grandfather and grandmother cannot be ruled out.

It is averred that from the DD No. 25 dated 26.10.2007, it is crystal clear that doctor from the hospital informed the police that Rambati @ Bittan has been brought to the hospital by neighbours who is brought dead.
It is averred that on the said information, Sub Inspector visited the hospital where plaintiff no. 2 was present but in shocked condition, she did not give her statement to the police.

It is averred that this fact was very much in the knowledge of the plaintiffs and that plaintiff no. 1 cleverly made another call to the police informing that "mere ladke ne apani patni ko maar diya hai".
It is averred that no statement was made by plaintiff no. 2 to the police that her son has killed his wife.

It is averred that the call was made to the police after a long gap of one hour and five minutes of the first information, although the police was very much there in the hospital as well as at the spot, only to create evidence to prove himself and his family members as innocent.

2.1 It is averred that it is clear from the statements that the deceased was brought by the neighbours in the hospital and not by the plaintiffs and that the instant suit is totally on concocted facts and circumstances.
It is averred that the suit is liable to be dismissed with heavy cost as plaintiffs succeeded to mislead the court while acquitting them from the offence.

It is averred that plaintiff no.
1 is very clever and disowned his son and also severed all his relations but at the time of incident, the plaintiffs were residing in the same and one house which proves that publication was published in the newspaper with malafide intention only to save their skin from the clutches of law.

It is averred that the defendant no. 1 has deposed about the demands made by the accused person and that a demand of Rs. 50,000/- was made in the month of June 2007 which could not be paid as the funds were not released by the department of defendant no. 1 upon his retirement till October 2007 and Rambati was killed.

It is averred that despite the demands, the defendants did not make any complaint against deceased Raj Kumar and plaintiffs as defendant no. 1 was teacher and was not interested to draw the parties into litigation as well as to save the married life of his daughter.
It is averred that opinion of the court is not reliable and it cannot be said that there was no demand of dowry from the side of plaintiffs.

It is averred that the deceased was having minor children and Raj Kumar has expired in jail therefore considering the welfare and bright future of minor children of deceased Rambati, the defendants did not file the appeal against the orders.
2.2 The defendants have denied that the plaintiffs and their family are very highly respectable person in the society and enjoy very good reputation as claimed.

It is also denied that defendants are person of pusillanimous & quarrelsome nature and have envy and jealousy with the plaintiff's family and that they have been harassing the plaintiffs in various manners as alleged.

It is submitted that PW-1 was eye witness of the incident but she was won over by the plaintiffs as she is still residing with the plaintiffs.
It is denied that false and baseless imputations were made by defendants with intention to injure and harm the plaintiffs' image or character.
It is averred that suit is liable to be dismissed with heavy cost.
3. In the replication filed to the written statement of the defendant, the plaintiff has reiterated and reaffirmed the averments made in the plaint.

It is denied that witness was won over by them during the trial and it is claimed that plaintiffs have been rightly and honourably acquitted by the court as they were innocent and falsely implicated by the defendants in collusion with the police officials.

Predecessor of this Court on 21.03.2016:-

Any other relief.
5. In support of case of their case, all the three plaintiffs appeared in the witness box.
On the other hand, despite having opportunities, the defendants have not examined either themselves or any witness to rebut the case of the plaintiffs.
6. I have heard the submissions made by Ld. Counsels for parties and have perused the file.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
Issue no. 1 Whether the suit filed by the plaintiff is not maintainable as he has suppressed the material facts and has not approached the court with clean hands ?
OPD Issue no. 2 Whether the plaintiff is entitled for recovery of damages for the malicious prosecution, as prayed for ?
OPP 7.
Both the issues are taken together for disposal as are interlinked.

The material findings for acquittal of the plaintiffs are mentioned in para 32 of judgment dated 23.10.2013 which is, for the sake of convenience is reproduced as under:-
"So far as the offence U/s 498A IPC against accused persons namely Om Prakash,
Ram Beti and Jitender are concerned, I would like to mention here that PW7 Desh Pal, father of deceased and PW17 Giriraj Singh, brother of deceased in their testimonies have deposed that accused persons used to demand motorcycle and television from deceased.
They have further deposed that accused persons had demanded Rs. 50,000/- from deceased at the time when PW7 had retired from his job in June 2007.

Admittedly deceased was married with accused Raj Kumar about 21 years ago and during her life time she had not lodged any complaint against accused Om Prakash, Ram Beti and Jitender with regard to alleged demand of dowry.
Even PW7 & 17 have leveled general allegations against the accused persons and they have not given any specific date, month or year when the alleged demand was raised by the accused persons.
It is also the plea of Ld. counsel for accused persons that accused Jitender was of about 5 years of age when at the time of marriage of Raj Kumar with deceased.

A specific suggestion was also put to PW7 in his cross examination regarding the age of Jitender but this witness neither admit nor deny the suggestion that accused Jitender was of 5-8 years at the time of marriage of his daughter.
In my view, the allegations leveled against the accused persons are highly improbable and it cannot be ruled out that accused persons namely Om Prakash,
Jitender
and Ram Beti have been roped in the present case because of their relationship with accused Raj Kumar

. Consequently, accused persons namely Om Prakash, Jitender and Ram Beti are acquitted under Section 498A IPC"
8.

The findings of the Ld. Additional Session Judge depicts that allegations levelled against the accused persons were viewed highly improbable and there is no finding of the Ld. Court that the allegations are false or that the accused persons, the plaintiffs of the present case have been roped into the case with malicious intent.
It is well settled principle of law that the only person who can be sued in an action for malicious prosecution is the person who prosecutes.

In the case in hand,
daughter in law of the plaintiff no. 1 and 2 was taken to the hospital by neighbours and the doctor reported the said fact to the police and that she was brought dead.
The police official reached to the hospital and before whom, plaintiff no. 2 appeared and was not able to give statement as was in shocked condition.
The police was also informed from K Block, House no. 43, Budh Vihar, Phase I that my son has murdered his wife.
Thus, the facts of the case depicts that the police was not put into motion by the defendants.

sentences.text: After investigation of the facts and finding the statement of defendants, it was the police officials who filed the final report in the form of chargesheet against the accused person.
The defendants have deposed during the trial and there is no finding as observed above of the trial court that they have deposed falsely.
Thus, the status of the defendants in the present case is merely of witnesses and not the prosecutors.

9. The plaintiffs in their oral testimony have re-iterated the pleadings and they have not brought on file any complaint filed by the defendants against them to establish that defendants were of quarrelsome nature and were envy and jealous with their family and were harassing their family members falsely and groundlessly.
There is no evidence brought by the plaintiffs on record that they were implicated by the defendants in any other litigation.

The plaintiffs have failed to establish the malice of the defendants while giving their statements to the police and deposing before the Ld.
Trial Court.

Considering the pleadings, testimony of the witnesses and the record, I am of view that the plaintiffs are not able to discharge their onus of the issue that they were prosecuted by the defendants maliciously.
The issues are decided accordingly.
Relief 10.
For the reasons discussed above, suit of the plaintiffs is dismissed.
No orders as to costs.
Decree sheet be prepared.
